name: Point Location Test
description: For each of q queries, given a directed line segment and a point, report whether the point is to the left, to the right, or exactly on the line through the segment.
why_hard: It's the pure orientation (cross-product) primitive everything else in this topic is built on — the recurring bug is off-by-sign errors between "left" and "right" depending on how the cross product is defined.

name: Line Segment Intersection
description: Given two line segments, determine whether they intersect and, if so, print the intersection point (or report that they overlap along a shared line).
why_hard: Requires correctly handling every degenerate case — collinear overlapping segments, touching endpoints, and segments that intersect at a single non-endpoint point — with exact integer/rational arithmetic rather than floating point.

name: Polygon Area
description: Given a simple polygon's vertices in order, compute twice its area (kept as an integer).
why_hard: Conceptually simple once you know the shoelace formula, but a common early mistake is forgetting to wrap the last vertex back to the first, or forgetting the factor of 2 the judge expects.

name: Point in Polygon
description: Given a simple polygon and several query points, classify each as inside, outside, or exactly on the boundary.
why_hard: The boundary case must be checked as a separate exact test before running the ray-casting parity test — ray-casting alone misclassifies points that lie exactly on an edge or vertex.

name: Minimum Euclidean Distance
description: Given n points, find the minimum distance between any two of them.
why_hard: The naive O(n^2) approach doesn't scale to CSES's constraints; the divide-and-conquer closest-pair algorithm (with the strip-check bounded by a packing argument) is the intended O(n log n)-ish solution.

name: Convex Hull
description: Given n points, output the vertices of their convex hull.
why_hard: Direct application of Andrew's monotone chain — the main risk is getting the collinear-point pop condition (<= vs <) wrong for whatever the judge's exact boundary convention is.

name: Maximum Manhattan Distances
description: Given n points, find the maximum Manhattan distance between any two of them.
why_hard: The O(n^2) pairwise approach is too slow; the intended trick is the 45-degree coordinate rotation (u=x+y, v=x-y) that turns Manhattan distance into Chebyshev distance, solvable with a single O(n) min/max scan.

name: Area of Rectangles
description: Given n axis-aligned rectangles, compute the total area they cover (overlaps counted once).
why_hard: Requires the coordinate-compression + sweep-line technique to merge covered y-intervals per x-slab; a segment-tree-based sweep is needed to pass the full constraint range in O(n log n).

name: Rectangle Area II
description: Given n axis-aligned rectangles, return the total area they cover modulo 1e9+7.
why_hard: Same sweep-line technique as Area of Rectangles, with the added bookkeeping of returning the answer modulo 1e9+7 — reported as a real question in this site's Company OA Bank (Squarepoint Capital).

name: Erect the Fence
description: Given the positions of trees in a garden, find the perimeter of the fence that can enclose all the trees, including any tree that lies exactly on the fence line.
why_hard: The one gotcha that trips up otherwise-correct convex hull code: collinear boundary points must be included in the output, unlike a standard strict convex hull — reported as a real question in this site's Company OA Bank at two different companies.
